newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Clinton pushes APEC on information technology trade.
newsitem.headline: Clinton pushes APEC on information technology trade.

text.p: President Clinton urged Asia-Pacific leaders Wednesday to spearhead their free trade push by cuting barriers in the $1 trillion-a-year information technology industry.

Clinton said that when leaders of Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum meet next week at their annual summit they must make progress toward their aim of ending all trade barriers in the region by 2020.
The president spoke to reporters after hour-long talks with Australian Prime Minister John Howard at which the pair discussed the need to maintain international momentum for cutting trade barriers.

"We know we have to keep this group working together to push the barriers that still restrain global trade and to work especially for opportunities that will enable our people to get better jobs, to lead better lives and in so doing to advance the cause of the other APEC nations as well," Clinton said. "The area that I would like to see the most progress in is in information technology."
The information technology industry, worth $1 trillion a year worldwide and projected to grow by 250 percent over the next decade, offered tremendous potential, Clinton said.
"We need to do more to open up those markets," he said.
The United States wants to substantially reduce import duties in the information technology industry, although it has not mentioned a schedule.

Clinton is seeking Asian backing to push the move through December's World Trade Organisation ministerial meeting in Singapore. U.S. Deputy National Security Adviser Samuel Berger said a strong endorsement by the 18-member APEC would have "a substantial impact."
Clinton's deputy assistant on economic policy, Daniel Tarullo, said in Washington last week information technology headed Clinton's APEC agenda.

"Our hope is that the (APEC) leaders as a whole will give the same kind of impetus toward moving ahead on an ITA (Information Technology Agreement) this year, as they did to the completion of the Uruguay Round (of trade talks) in 1993," Tarullo said.
Clinton said improved global communications through new technology would minimise misunderstandings and help create a more peaceful world.

Clinton arrived in Australia Tuesday on his first trip abroad since being re-elected this month and his first visit to Australia, a close U.S. regional ally, ahead of the APEC summit at Subic Bay in the Philippines.

"It is very, very important, now that we have a goal of free trade in the area by 2020 ... that we actually take some concrete steps toward implementation of our goal from tariff cuts to other deregulation measures," Clinton said.
"I will be working hard for that."
The APEC free trade pact, struck at the 1994 summit in Indonesia, binds developed members to dropping all trade barriers by 2010 and developing economies by 2020.

APEC groups Australia, Brunei, Canada, Chile, China, Hong Kong, Indonesia, Japan, South Korea, Malaysia, Mexico, New Zealand, Papua New Guinea, the Philippines, Singapore, Taiwan, Thailand and the United States.
